text:
morgan: Heads up — EVR POC asked for a signed pen-test attestation and ISO/SOC2 artifacts. They want: a) a pen-test letter signed by our security lead, b) staging access for their security team, and c) confirmation whether Redwood will run the external scan or if customer runs it. Timeline: they need the letter + upload link by next Tue (7 business days).

sam: thx. do we have an internal template for the pen-test letter or do we need legal? also any cost implications if we provide staging access / dedicated nodes?

rachel: we have a standard pen-test attestation template (minimal) but anything needing signature by security lead should be routed through legal for final wording. biggest question: who owns remediation if the customer runs the scan vs if we run it. we normally accept "notify-only" scans on staging but for prod we require coordinated red-team with scope.

alex: technical note — if we give them staging access we can provide ephemeral bastion + readonly logs. for uploads we prefer presigned S3 or SFTP. presigned is easiest:

```
aws s3 presign s3://redwood-poc-evidence/evr/pen-test-letter.pdf --expires-in 604800
```

sam: ok. pricing side — if they want dedicated pool or extra burst capacity for the POC scans (external scans can generate lots of token usage and KV cache churn), sales should flag that. For a 2-week POC with heavy scanning we typically add a short-term reserved capacity line item.

morgan: EVR's security lead specifically said "we need Redwood to sign a pen-test attestation, and we may request Redwood-run external scanning for end-to-end coverage". So two asks: 1) signature & upload path, 2) quote for short-term dedicated capacity + staging creds.

rachel: action items from sec side: I can sign the attestation once legal approves the language. if customer requests Redwood-run scan we need scope, IP ranges, and a signed PO. also we should provide a redacted logs policy and confirm KMS separation for staging (no customer keys in our shared staging).

alex: for staging KMS — we can spin up a tenant-isolated staging with customer-specific encryption keys, but that triggers Dedicated/Private pricing (short-term reserved = possible). if they accept presigned upload + our attestation, we can avoid the customer-managed KMS ask.

sam: can someone ballpark the cost delta for a 2-week reserved burst? i.e., add 4 GPUs of dedicated for 2 weeks. sales planning needs a number to include in quote.

morgan: customer asked for a rough number ASAP (EOD tomorrow). they want to know if the POC will push them into Dedicated pricing domain.

alex: very rough — short-term reserved for 4 A10Gs for 2 weeks = around $8k–12k depending on region and burst config. (very rough; will get exact).

rachel: also confirm data handling: any evidence we share should have IPs redacted unless they sign an NDA. we should attach our minimal SOC2 artifact list (control owners + evidence links) rather than full reports.

morgan: path forward suggested: 1) sam include provisional cost for 2-week reserved burst in the quote (label as estimate), 2) rachel draft pen-test attestation + list of artifacts we can provide, route to legal for signature, 3) alex prepare presigned S3 bucket + ephemeral bastion plan and a short runbook for customer-run scans.

sam: will add estimate to quote and mark as provisional. will also ask finance for an exact short-term reserved SKU by EOD.

rachel: I'll draft attestation now and ping legal. quick Q: do we have a standard redaction checklist for logs?

alex: yes — redact IPs, full user tokens, PII fields. we can provide anonymized traces and event ids.

security-bot: reminder: attach SOC2 artifact index: https://intra.redwood/company/security/soc2-index (internal link).

morgan: thanks all — I'll feed this back to EVR and ask them to confirm whether they want Redwood to run the scan or provide own scan creds. will post updates here. :thumbsup:
